note: Financial terminology for the knowledge base and for Gemma 4's grounding. Written in the SME role for carddemo (credit cards), zopeneditor-sample (customer master maintenance) and fineract-legacy (Apache Fineract progressive loan schedules); awaiting the owner's confirmation. aliases are natural-language phrases; codeTerms are identifier fragments as they appear in COBOL or Java (matched by sub-words, so LT-ANNUAL-RATE and annualRate both match ANNUAL-RATE). functions are taxonomy.json classes; weight (default 1) lowers generic terms.

terms.definition: A sum of money lent to a borrower and repaid, with interest, through a schedule of installments.
The amount lent, or the part of it still owed excluding interest, fees and penalties. Interest is calculated on principal.

The parameters that drive a loan's schedule: principal, number of repayments, repayment frequency, nominal interest rate, interest method, amortization type, day-count conventions, currency and rounding.
How long the loan runs: the number of repayments times the repayment frequency, or a fixed number of days.
How many installments the schedule has; with the frequency it fixes the due dates.
How often installments fall due: a unit (days, weeks, months, years) and a count ('repay every 2 weeks').
The yearly rate quoted for the loan, in percent, before it is converted into a rate for a period or a day. It excludes compounding and fees.
The charge for borrowing money, computed from a balance, a rate and a period; in these estates it is simple interest per period (CardDemo monthly, Fineract per interest period).
The price of borrowing, as a percentage of the balance per period (per year unless stated).
The annual rate converted to one repayment period, for example the annual rate divided by 12 for monthly installments.
The annual rate divided by the days in the year (the day-count basis). Daily interest is balance × daily rate × days.

In Fineract's progressive EMI calculator, the share of the nominal annual rate that applies to one interest period: rate × (days in the period ÷ days in the year) for day-based frequencies, or rate × period fraction ÷ periods per year for week- and month-based ones. Interest = balance × rate factor, and the EMI is computed from the rate factors.
The part of a full repayment period that an interest period or a partial period covers (actual days ÷ days of the full period). It scales the periodic rate.
The day-count basis of the year used to turn an annual rate into a daily one: actual (365 or 366), 360, 364 or 365.
The day-count basis of a month: actual calendar days or 30.
The rules for counting the days between two dates and in a year when interest is calculated (for example Actual/365, Actual/360, 30/360).

The constant installment that repays the principal and interest of a declining-balance loan over its term. Each EMI covers the period's interest; the rest reduces principal. For a constant periodic rate r and n periods: EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n − 1).
One scheduled payment due on a due date: principal plus interest, and any fees and penalties.
A product setting that rounds the installment amount to a multiple of a currency amount (for example to the nearest 10). It is separate from rounding to the currency's decimal places.
Paying off a loan through scheduled installments that pay interest and reduce principal: equal installments (EMI) or equal principal payments.
An interest method where each period's interest is computed on the outstanding principal, which falls as it is repaid.
An interest method where interest is computed on the original principal for the whole term, whatever has been repaid.
How interest is computed for the loan: declining balance or flat.
The interval between two due dates; each one produces one installment. In Fineract's model it holds its interest periods, EMI, principal and interest due and paid.
A sub-interval of a repayment period with one balance and one rate. Interest is computed per interest period and summed; a disbursement or a rate change starts a new one.
The date by which an installment must be paid; it ends a repayment period.
The first day of a repayment or interest period (the previous period's due date).
The due date of the last installment, when the loan should be fully repaid.
The table of installments of a loan: for each period its dates, principal, interest, fees, penalties, total due and outstanding balance.
Fineract's component that turns loan terms into a repayment schedule; in the COBOL estate it is FNLS0100 (job FNSCHGEN).
The generated schedule as Fineract returns it: periods with amounts and totals, then mapped to a plan for output.
Fineract's loan schedule type in which installments are computed period by period by an EMI calculator over an interest schedule model, so the schedule can be recalculated as events happen.
The in-memory model of repayment periods and their interest periods that the EMI calculator reads and updates (FNMODEL in the COBOL estate).
Fineract's calculator for progressive loans: rate factors, EMI, balances, disbursements and recalculation over the interest schedule model (FNEM0100–FNEM0900 in the COBOL estate).
What the borrower still owes at a point in time: principal not yet repaid (and, depending on context, unpaid interest, fees and penalties).
The part of an installment that repays principal: installment minus the period's interest (and fees).
The part of an installment that pays the interest accrued in its period.
Everything due on a due date: principal + interest + fees + penalties.
Amounts of a repayment period computed from others rather than stored, such as principal due = EMI − interest due, or the balance after the period.
Paying the loan funds out to the borrower. It creates or increases the outstanding principal from its date, and can split a repayment period into interest periods.
One of several partial disbursements of the same loan.
A Fineract option where each tranche is repaid over the full loan term instead of the remaining periods.
A portion of the disbursed principal (a percentage of the disbursement) that is due on the disbursement date as a separate schedule line, reducing the principal the installments repay.
The date funds are (expected to be) paid out; interest on them starts from it.
The date from which due dates are generated, usually the disbursement or submission date; each due date is the seed plus k × the repayment frequency.
Periods during which principal (or interest) is not repaid; the deferred amount is spread over the later installments.
Recomputing interest and installments from the actual balances and dates (for example till a given date) instead of the original plan.

terms.term: EMI adjustment of the last period
terms.definition: Changing the EMI of the last unpaid period so the schedule repays the principal exactly, absorbing the rounding residue of earlier installments.
Fineract's iteration that adjusts the EMI so the installments of the related periods come out equal after rounding, with only the last one absorbing the difference.
A Fineract option that fixes the loan's length in days, so the last period ends on the fixed day even if it is shorter than a full period.
A Fineract option to start interest on the disbursement date itself rather than the following day.
Whether interest of a partial (broken) period is computed on its actual days rather than as a full period.
An amount charged in addition to interest (for example a processing fee). The Tier 1 schedules carry zero fees; the charge passes still run.
A charge for late or missed payment.
The input record asking for a schedule: loan id, disbursement amount and date, number of repayments, frequency, rate and options.
The money unit of the amounts, with its ISO code and its number of decimal places, to which money amounts are rounded.
Fineract's amount type: a BigDecimal amount with a currency and a math context. Its arithmetic (plus, minus, multipliedBy, dividedBy) rounds to the currency's decimal places.
Fineract's helper for null-safe BigDecimal arithmetic, percentages and comparisons.
Java's MathContext: a precision (significant digits) and a rounding mode that BigDecimal operations apply to their results. The run control record sets it for the COBOL estate.
The rule for discarding digits: HALF_EVEN, HALF_UP, HALF_DOWN, UP, DOWN, CEILING or FLOOR.
Round to the nearest value; an exact half goes to the even neighbour (2.5 → 2, 3.5 → 4). It avoids the upward bias of HALF_UP over many amounts and is Fineract's usual money rounding.
Round to the nearest value; an exact half goes away from zero (2.5 → 3, −2.5 → −3). COBOL's ROUNDED phrase rounds this way by default.
Round to the nearest value; an exact half goes toward zero (2.5 → 2).

terms.term: UP, DOWN, CEILING and FLOOR rounding
terms.definition: UP rounds away from zero, DOWN toward zero (truncation), CEILING toward +∞ and FLOOR toward −∞, whatever the discarded digits.
The number of digits after the decimal point (BigDecimal scale; the digits after V in a COBOL PICTURE).
The digits of a number from the first non-zero one; a math context's precision limits how many are kept.
value × percentage ÷ 100, computed with the math context (MathUtil.percentageOf); for example the down payment from its percentage.

The COBOL estate's arithmetic subprograms that reproduce Java BigDecimal exactly: FNDKRND rounds an unscaled integer to a scale or to significant digits, FNDKDFO multiplies, divides and adds decimal floating values (coefficient and exponent), FNDTKRN does date arithmetic.
A decimal number held as an integer coefficient and a power of ten: value = coefficient × 10^exponent (BigDecimal: unscaled value × 10^−scale).
Dropping digits without rounding. COBOL stores a result truncated to the receiving PICTURE unless ROUNDED is coded.
Mainframe formats for exact decimal amounts: packed (two digits per byte and a sign nibble) and zoned (one digit per byte, the sign overpunched in the last byte).
In PIC 9(9)V99 the V marks where the decimal point is assumed; no point is stored, so 12345 in V99 means 123.45.
A result too large for its receiving field. Without ON SIZE ERROR, COBOL silently drops the high-order digits.
A date held as a count of days from an epoch (COBOL FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE, Java LocalDate.toEpochDay), so the difference of two dates is a day count.
The number of days from one date to another (ChronoUnit.DAYS.between); the basis of actual-day interest.
The last calendar day of a month (28 to 31); due dates that fall past it are clamped to it.
A year of 366 days (divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400); actual/actual day counts change in it.
Moving a date by whole months clamps to the last valid day (31 January + 1 month = 28 or 29 February); next due dates are computed this way.
Checking that a date has a valid format and value; CardDemo's CSUTLDTC calls the Language Environment service CEEDAYS.
Date and time of an event; CardDemo transactions carry when they originated (TRAN-ORIG-TS) and when they were processed (TRAN-PROC-TS).
The date and time the program reads from the system (FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE, ACCEPT FROM DATE); tests pin it so outputs are repeatable.
The account a card draws on (ACCOUNT-RECORD): current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, cycle credit and debit, status, open, expiry and reissue dates, and the account group.
A payment card: number, CVV, embossed name, expiry date and status, linked to an account.
The record linking a card number to its customer id and account id (CARD-XREF-RECORD); posting uses it to find the account of a transaction's card.
The maximum balance allowed on the account. CardDemo rejects a transaction whose amount would take cycle credits − cycle debits + amount past it (reason 102, overlimit).
The part of the credit limit that may be drawn as cash advances.
The account's balance now (ACCT-CURR-BAL): posting adds each transaction amount (purchases positive, payments and credits negative).
The total of positive transaction amounts posted in the current billing cycle (ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT); CardDemo adds an amount here when it is ≥ 0.
The total of negative transaction amounts posted in the current billing cycle (ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT).
The period between two statements; cycle credits and debits accumulate over it.
Whether the account is active (Y) or not.
The date after which the account may not be used; CardDemo rejects a transaction whose origination date is after it (reason 103). The copybook spells the field ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE.
When the account's cards were last reissued.

The group id on the account that selects its interest rates in the disclosure group file (DISCGRP), keyed by group, transaction type and category. CardDemo falls back to the DEFAULT group when the account's group has no rate.
A financial event on a card or account: purchase, payment, credit, fee or interest, with an amount, a type and category, a merchant and timestamps (TRAN-RECORD).
The day's incoming transactions (DALYTRAN), read and posted by CBTRN02C.
A code classifying the transaction (for example purchase or payment). With the category code it keys category balances and interest rates.
A finer classification under the transaction type (TRAN-CAT-CD).
The balance of one account per transaction type and category (TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD). Posting adds each transaction to it (creating the record if missing); interest is computed on it.
Recording a validated transaction: writing it to the transaction master and updating the account balance, cycle totals and category balance.

CardDemo's interest for one category balance: balance × annual rate (percent) ÷ 1200, that is ÷ 100 for percent and ÷ 12 for a month. The account's total interest is added to its current balance and written as an interest transaction.
A system-generated transaction (SYSTRAN) that charges computed interest to the account.

A code and text explaining why an input was not processed. CardDemo: 100 invalid card number, 101 account not found, 102 overlimit, 103 transaction after account expiration. Fineract COBOL: a reject record per loan request with code, source and text.
A transaction that would take the account past its credit limit; CardDemo rejects it with reason 102.
The business where a card transaction took place (id, name, city, zip).
A periodic document listing an account's transactions and balances; CardDemo prints it in CBSTM03A (text and HTML).
A printed list of transactions in a date range with page, account and grand totals (CardDemo CBTRN03C, job TRANREPT).
Sums printed at the end of a page, at a change of account (control break) and at the end of the report.
Paying the account balance in full online (COBIL00C): a payment transaction is written and the account balance is reduced by the amount.
The decision to approve or decline a card transaction at the point of sale, before it is posted.
A person who holds accounts and cards (CardDemo CUSTOMER-RECORD), or a record of the SAM customer master file.
A credit-worthiness score (300–850) kept on the CardDemo customer record.
A personal identifier on the customer record; sensitive data.
Applying a sorted transaction file to a sorted customer master file by key and writing a new master with the changes (SAM1); unmatched and bad transactions are reported.
A SAM transaction that inserts a new, blank customer record with the given key.
A SAM transaction that changes one field of a customer record: REPLACE sets it, ADD and SUBTRACT change a numeric amount (SAM2 applies it).
A SAM transaction that removes the customer record with the given key from the new master.
Contact data of a customer (name, address, phone); in SAM a second record type of the customer file.
SAM1's 132-column print report: a line per transaction with its result, then totals of records read, added, updated and deleted and of transactions in error.
An entry on the left side of an account; on a card account, a charge that increases what the customer owes.
An entry on the right side of an account; on a card account, a payment or refund that decreases what the customer owes.
The book of accounts in which postings are recorded.
Recognizing interest as it is earned day by day, before it is due or paid.
The net amount of an account at a point in time.
The yearly cost of credit as a percentage, including interest and some fees; distinct from the nominal rate.
Interest on the principal only: principal × rate × time. CardDemo's monthly interest and Fineract's per-period interest are simple interest on the period's balance.
Interest on principal plus previously added interest; the EMI formula assumes per-period compounding of the periodic rate.
Installments due and not paid; the overdue amount and days past due drive penalties and provisioning.
Repaying principal ahead of the schedule, which reduces later interest or installments.
The order in which a payment is applied to penalties, fees, interest and principal.
The FNSTAT block every Fineract subprogram returns: ST-OK, or a reject code and text. A Java exception (for example the FLAT interest method's throw) becomes a reject of the loan request.
Checking input against rules before processing it, and rejecting or reporting what fails.
Text returned to the caller or shown on screen when an input or operation fails.
The two-character code each file operation returns: '00' success, '10' end of file, '23' record not found, '35' file missing.
The condition when a sequential read finds no more records; batch loops stop on it.
An abnormal end: the program stops with an abend code (through CEE3ABD) after a severe error, such as a file that cannot be opened.
The value a program returns to its job step; the job's MAXCC is the highest. CardDemo POSTTRAN returns 4 when transactions were rejected; SAM1 sets 16 on file errors.
Job Control Language describes a batch job's steps, the program each runs and the datasets (DD statements) it reads and writes.
A mainframe file, named by its DSN and bound to a program's file by a DD statement.
A keyed file whose records are read, written and rewritten by key (and optionally alternate keys).
Parameters of a batch run: a control record (Fineract: math context precision and rounding mode) or the JCL PARM (CardDemo INTCALC: the run date).
Counts of records read, written, posted and rejected, displayed or printed at the end of the run.
Authenticating a user id and password against the user security file before showing the menu (CardDemo COSGN00C).
A user's id, name, password and type (admin or regular) in the USRSEC file; admins can add, update, delete and list users.
The online screen that lists the functions a user may run and transfers control to the chosen program.
IBM's transaction monitor for online screens; CardDemo's CO* programs are CICS programs that send and receive BMS maps and pass state in the COMMAREA.
Writing records to an interchange file and reading them back elsewhere (CardDemo CBEXPORT and CBIMPORT for branch migration).
The utility that defines, deletes and copies VSAM and sequential files; jobs use REPRO to load and unload files.
Ordering records by key (DFSORT or the COBOL SORT verb), for example transactions before a report or a master update.
